response.sql: WITH qualifying AS (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(`U-PRO`) <> '' AND `U-PRO` <> '-'), lab_in_patient AS (SELECT l.ID, l.PT, CAST(l.ALP AS REAL) / l.GPT AS ALP_GPT FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM qualifying)), per_patient AS (SELECT ID, AVG(PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(ALP_GPT) AS avg_alp_gpt FROM lab_in_patient GROUP BY ID) SELECT COALESCE(p.SEX, '') AS SEX, AVG(pp.avg_pt) AS avg_PT, AVG(pp.avg_alp_gpt) AS avg_ALP_GPT_ratio FROM per_patient pp JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = pp.ID GROUP BY COALESCE(p.SEX, '');

assumptions.assumption: A U-PRO value is 'recorded' when it is not NULL and not an empty or whitespace-only string; any other value (e.g. '+', '±', '1+') counts unless it is exactly '-'.
Each patient's averages use all of that patient's lab records, not only the records where U-PRO is recorded; the qualifying U-PRO condition only selects which patients are included.
ALP ÷ GPT uses real-valued division (ALP is cast to REAL) so integer truncation does not occur; records with GPT = 0 or a NULL ALP/GPT produce NULL and are ignored by AVG.
Blank sex means SEX is NULL or '', and both are grouped together and returned as an empty-string SEX value.
